label: Lipoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Lipoma is the most common soft tissue tumor, presenting as a soft, benign, well-circumscribed mass.
- Commonly occurs in the upper back, proximal extremities, and abdominal region.
- Histologically composed of mature adipocytes without atypical features or lipoblasts.
- Exclusion of MDM2 amplification is important for deep-seated or retroperitoneal lipomas >10 cm ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)).
- Differential diagnosis includes well-differentiated liposarcoma, spindle cell lipoma, myofibroblastoma, and hibernoma.

## Terminology
- Lipoma: benign tumor of mature adipocytes.
- No synonyms recommended ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)).

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Composed of mature adipocytes without atypia or lipoblasts ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Lipoma.html)).
- **Desirable:**
  - Rare cytogenetic findings may include 12q13-15 rearrangements, HMGA2 overexpression absent in synovial lipomatosis ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)).

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:**
  - Common soft tissue tumor, typically in adults.
  - Can occur superficially or deep-seated ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)).
- **Site:**
  - Occurs frequently in upper back, proximal extremities, abdominal region.
  - Intramuscular lipomas often in the thigh (40–50%) ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)).
- **Presentation:**
  - Painless, soft, mobile mass.
- **Prognosis:**
  - Excellent, with no risk of malignancy in typical cases.
- **Synovial Lipomatosis:**
  - Proliferation of lipomatous tissue in joints, often associated with chronic joint disease, lacking HMGA2 overexpression ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)).

## Macroscopic
- Typically well-circumscribed, encapsulated yellowish mass.
- Size varies widely but often small ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html)).

## Microscopic
- Sheet-like proliferation of mature adipocytes.
- Possibly fibrous septa but devoid of atypical hyperchromatic stromal cells.
- May include fat necrosis or dystrophic calcification in some cases ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Lipoma.html)).

![Histological sections show a homogeneous population of mature adipocytes.](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_PICS/BST/5372.jpg)

## Ancillary Tests
- **IHC/molecular:**
  - Molecular testing generally not required.
  - Exclusion of MDM2 amplification is significant for tumors >10 cm or deep-seated ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html)).

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Spindle Cell Lipoma:**
  - Contains spindle cells, myxoid stroma, CD34 positive ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueaslt.html)).
- **Well-differentiated Liposarcoma:**
  - Features atypical stromal cells, lipoblasts, and MDM2 amplification ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissuewdliposarcoma.html)).
- **Hibernoma:**
  - Comprised of multivacuolated eosinophilic fat cells, distinguishable by its metabolically active fat ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposehibernoma.html)).
- **Chondroid Lipoma:**
  - Contains chondroid stroma and myxoid matrix ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposechondroid.html)).
- **Myofibroblastoma:**
  - Spindle cell lesion with overlapping features with other spindle cell entities ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)).
- **Desmoid-type Fibromatosis:**
  - Aggressive fibrous tissue proliferation ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)).
- **Fat-forming or Lipomatous Solitary Fibrous Tumour:**
  - Fatty tumor with solitary fibrous tumor features ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)).
- **Silicon Granuloma:**
  - Reaction to foreign bodies ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)).
- **Signet-ring Cell Carcinoma:**
  - Tumor with signet-ring cell morphology ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)).
- **Balloon Cell Melanoma:**
  - Melanoma variant with balloon cells ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)).
- **Perivascular Epithelioid Cell Tumour (PEComa):**
  - Tumor with epithelioid and perivascular features ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html)).

cards.excerpt: Entity: Lipoma Section: localization Lipomas are most common in the upper back, proximal extremity, and abdominal region, and the majority present as a superficial (subcutaneous) soft tissue mass. A smaller subset are deep-seated, arising within skeletal muscle (intramuscular lipoma), on the surface of bone (parosteal lipoma), or within the tendon sheath, or they may involve the gastrointestinal tract, oral cavity, or bronchial tree. Intramuscular lipomas most frequently involve the thigh (40–50%), followed by the shoulder, chest wall, and upper limb. Rare examples of retroperitoneal lipomas with cytogenetic and molecular confirmation have also been reported. Synovial lipomatosis (lipoma arborescens) is a lipomatous proliferation of subsynovial connective tissue often associated with chronic joint disease, and recent work has shown that this adipocytic proliferation lacks HMGA2 overexpression, supporting a non-neoplastic reactive process.

Spindle cell lipomas overlap with other spindle cell lesions of the soft tissue (e.g. myofibroblastoma and desmoid-type fibromatosis) and fat-forming or lipomatous solitary fibrous tumour. Less common entities included in the differential diagnosis are silicon granuloma and neoplasms with clear cell features, such as signet-ring cell carcinoma, balloon cell melanoma, and perivascular epithelioid cell tumour (PEComa).

Painless, subcutaneous mass
In special site, might have specific symptoms (i.e. gastrointestinal → melena)
5% multiple (Acta Orthop Scand 1983;54:929)
Cowden syndrome (J Med Genet 1999;36:360)
Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndrome (GeneReviews: PTEN Hamartoma Tumor Syndrome [Accessed 18 November 2021])

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Epidemiology
cards.excerpt:
Commonly affects middle aged to elderly men (45 - 70 years) (Cancer 1975;36:1852)
Very rare in patients < 20 years
< 10% of cases occur in women
Uncommon compared with conventional lipoma (ratio = 1:60)

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Sites
cards.excerpt:
Mostly superficial, extremely rare in deep soft tissue
80% arise in the subcutaneous tissue of the posterior neck, back and shoulders (Cancer 1975;36:1852, Cancer 1981;47:126)
20% involve different sites, including face, oral cavity and trunk / extremities (Acta Pathol Microbiol Scand A 1976;84:477, Histopathology 1987;11:803, Histopathology 2015;66:430, Am J Clin Pathol 2016;146:487)
Cases in women more likely to arise in atypical locations (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:1267)
Intramuscular and dermal based lesions rarely seen (Am J Clin Pathol 2016;146:487, Am J Dermatopathol 2000;22:496)

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Characterized by partial or whole chromosome 13 or 16 deletions (Histopathology 1997;31:222)
Breakpoints cluster around 13q14 where the RB1 gene resides (Int J Cancer 2003;103:616)
Part of the so called 13q / RB1 family of tumors, which includes myofibroblastoma and cellular angiofibroma (Hum Pathol 2012;43:1887, Am J Surg Pathol 2016;40:3617, Mod Pathol 2011;24:82)

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Myxoid background with mast cells frequent
cards.excerpt:
Short and stubby spindle cells show occasional palisading
Rare lipoblasts present in half of cases (Hum Pathol 2017;65:140)
Infiltrative growth, necrosis, atypical spindle cells, pleomorphic lipoblasts and significant mitotic activity usually absent (Semin Diagn Pathol 2019;36:105)
Fat poor and fat free subtype: contains little (< 5%) to no fat (Am J Dermatopathol 2007;29:437, Am J Dermatopathol 2009;31:423)
Myxoid subtype: contains abundant myxoid stroma (Pathol Int 2014;64:346)
(Pseudo) angiomatous subtype: contains dilated endothelial lined channels and nodules of floating tumor (Histopathology 1994;24:565, Pathol Int 2007;57:26)
Plexiform variant has been described (Histopathology 1995;27:533)
Focal cartilaginous and osseous metaplasia rarely present (Histopathology 1987;11:803)
Extramedullary hematopoiesis may occur (Histopathology 2001;39:215)

cards.title: Chondroid lipoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Shows recurrent t(11;16)(q13;p13) translocation with resultant C11orf95 and MRTFB fusion (Genes Chromosomes Cancer 2010;49:810)
Megakaryoblastic leukemia 2 (MKL2) / myocardin related transcription factor B (MRTFB) acts as coactivator of transcription factor serum response factor (SRF)

cards.title: Chondroid lipoma — Radiology description
cards.excerpt:
CT typically shows a well defined, heterogeneously enhancing mass with variable areas of fat attenuation
Can exhibit calcification and ossification on radiographs (Australas Med J 2012;5:355, Skeletal Radiol 2004;33:670)
MRI usually shows a well defined mass with lobulated areas of T2 hyperintense or fluid-like signal intensity (Balkan Med J 2015;32:107, Skeletal Radiol 1996;25:592)
Appears isointense or hypointense to muscle, with focal hyperintense areas (fat areas) on T1 weighted MR images
